review_scope: Exact full-resolution review of all three 4x2 vocabulary reference boards, all 24 literal vocabulary-panel crops, the selected ten picture-book crops, and both picture-book masters after a targeted fork/knife repair.

checks: every crop contains exactly one complete target object
cup handle and stemless drinking-glass boundary remain explicit
plate is shallow and bowl is visibly deep
spoon bowl, four fork tines, and blunt knife blade remain distinct
no text, logos, people, food, liquid, or competing table object appears
rejections: The original storyboard master's fork/knife middle transitions were not accepted because the active utensil silhouette was ambiguous; dedicated replacement panels were generated and reviewed.

checks: every selected page preserves exactly one cup, plate, spoon, bowl, fork, knife, drinking glass, and napkin
pages 2-9 show exactly one active object in frozen order
page 6 shows four unmistakable fork tines and page 7 shows an untined blunt knife blade
initial and terminal pages preserve the complete event states
every extraction follows an intentional panel border and retains the whole scene
no learner-facing text, character, hand, food, or extra tableware appears

crop_decision: All crops follow intentional contact-sheet or storyboard panel borders. Vocabulary crops isolate one complete object because neighboring panels would be competing answers; story crops retain every object and the entire event context.
